highlight.title: What Really Happens When You Type a URL and Hit Enter
highlight.summary: <cite index="12-2,12-18,12-30,12-34">Modern browsers route DNS queries through encrypted channels automatically, resolve the IP address, then use either HTTP/3 with QUIC protocol which combines transport and TLS handshakes into a single step, or fall back to TCP with traditional TLS 1.3 encryption.</cite> <cite index="12-39,12-6">HTTP/3 can be up to four times faster than HTTP/1.1 on mobile networks, with edge computing moving code closer to users and encrypted DNS protecting browsing habits by default.</cite>

resources.title: Introduction to Networking for Complete Beginners
resources.why_now: <cite index="5-17,5-20">This course teaches elementary networking concepts in 60 minutes and is currently free for a limited time.</cite> <cite index="5-4,5-14">Over 250,000 students have joined this beginner-friendly training that covers basic commands like ipconfig, ping and traceroute.</cite>

resources.title: BGP Vortex: Internet Routing Vulnerabilities Create Outages
resources.why_now: <cite index="21-8,21-17">Research published in January 2026 reveals that 21 of the 30 largest internet networks are susceptible to BGP Vortex attacks, which could impact 96% of all internet networks if triggered.</cite> <cite index="21-19">Lab experiments show these attacks can delay route propagation from near-instant to 40 seconds, causing communication outages.</cite>

resources.title: HTTP/3 and QUIC Protocol Complete Guide 2026
resources.why_now: <cite index="31-6,31-8,31-9">HTTP/3 fundamentally changes web transport by using QUIC protocol built on UDP instead of TCP, where head-of-line blocking occurs at stream level rather than connection level, allowing other streams to continue when one experiences packet loss.</cite> <cite index="31-12,31-13">QUIC provides built-in encryption for all packets, unlike TCP where encryption is optional.</cite>

resources.title: Cloudflare Route Leak Incident Analysis - January 22, 2026
resources.why_now: <cite index="30-18,30-19,30-20">This real-world BGP route leak case study from January 2026 shows how a 25-minute misconfiguration accidentally funneled external traffic through Cloudflare's Miami data center, causing congestion and elevated latency.</cite> <cite index="30-17">The incident involved Type 3 and Type 4 route leaks according to RFC7908 definitions.</cite>

claude_take: 2026 is fascinating because we're seeing the internet's foundational protocols evolve in real-time - encrypted DNS is now default, HTTP/3 is gaining serious traction, and yet BGP vulnerabilities like the Vortex attack remind us that our 30-year-old routing infrastructure still has critical flaws. The gap between cutting-edge protocol improvements and legacy system vulnerabilities perfectly illustrates why understanding both layers is essential for anyone working with networks today.
